# <box-name> <incus-state> <scenario>   — see test/stub-box
#
# A SMALL fleet for the cli/crew roster-loop tests, deliberately separate from
# fixtures/fleet.txt: that one contains `ff-wedged`, whose exec never answers
# (the collector must time out on it), and cli/crew has no probe timeout — one
# wedged box would hang the suite for two minutes per call.
#
# What is here is what the roster loops must survive: a hired box, a stopped
# one, one never hired, one whose logins are dead, and one that is not on the
# host at all. Every row exercises a different branch of `crew status`.
# Hired seconds ago, armed, credentials fine — and no ~/duty/duty.log yet,
# because nothing has run. FIRST on purpose: this is the row that used to end
# `crew status` outright (#224), and only a fixture that puts it AHEAD of a
# healthy box can tell a real fix from one that repairs the note alone.
cli-neverticked running  neverticked
cli-hired      running  working
cli-idle       running  idle
cli-suppressed running  suppressed
cli-supp-silent running suppressed-silent
cli-supp-unknown running suppressed-unknown
cli-supp-working running suppressed-working
cli-supp-stuck running suppressed-stuck
cli-stuck      running  stuck
cli-supp-nots running suppressed-notimestamp
cli-supp-old-orphan running suppressed-old-orphan
cli-supp-paired running suppressed-paired-crash
cli-silent     running  silent
# Present on the host and answering nothing. It must stay distinguishable from
# the never-ticked box above: both have no duty log, and only one of them is
# fine (#224 criterion 4, #221 one call site over).
cli-unreachable running  unreachable
cli-stopped    stopped  working
cli-nothired   running  nothired
cli-noauth     running  noauth
cli-absent     absent   working
# Hired, has ticked, and its crontab holds no live tick.sh line — the shape
# `crew status` could not describe at all before #189.
cli-disarmed   running  disarmed
# The reported case (#220): `rig bootstrap` FAILED, so /etc/rig/role was never
# written and the vendor CLI was never installed. Reachable, running, and
# un-hired — indistinguishable from cli-nothired above in every column crew
# had, which is exactly why the table invited the operator to hire it.
cli-unconverged running  unconverged
# Converged, un-hired, and built by a rig older than /etc/rig/manifest (rig#61)
# — the marker is there, the provenance file is not. It exists to hold the
# corroborating-only rule down: a box missing `converged_at` is `converged`, so
# gating on the manifest would turn every box on an older rig into a refusal,
# which #220's own test plan calls the outcome worse than the bug.
cli-premanifest running  premanifest
# A `build` in flight declaring the 3600s ceiling roles/builder.conf gives that
# lane, on three boxes whose only difference is the lock age: 40 minutes,
# exactly ceiling-plus-kill-grace, and one second past it. Before #624 all
# three read STUCK in `crew status` at ten minutes while the floor called the
# first two healthy — two consoles, one box, two answers.
cli-lane-build running  lane-build
cli-lane-edge  running  lane-edge
cli-lane-over  running  lane-over
# An engine older than the `timeout=` token: there is no ceiling to read, so
# both readers fall back to STUCK_AFTER_S. This is the box that must not move.
cli-lane-legacy running  lane-legacy
# The same quartet's question asked of a ceiling the two readers' LANGUAGES
# disagree about: `timeout=0900s`, which Python reads as 900 and bash reads as
# an invalid octal literal. Not a wrong badge — an ABORT. The arithmetic is
# fatal under `set -euo pipefail`, so `crew status` stopped printing at this
# box and took every row below it with it, which is why these two sit ABOVE
# `cli-unconverged` and `cli-premanifest` rather than at the end of the file.
cli-lane-zero  running  lane-zero
cli-lane-zero-over running lane-zero-over
